Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the all-important chase! If India Women manage to gun this down, it will be their highest-ever run-chase in WODIs, but standing in front of them is the unbeaten England Women side, who will be eager to secure their semifinal spot in this game only. Here come the England players who spread out and take their respective field positions. Pratika Rawal and Smriti Mandhana are the two openers for India. Lauren Bell to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

India Women managed to pull things back towards the latter stages of the innings, with their bowling attack showing some resilience. Deepti Sharma was the standout performer with her four vital wickets. Charani provided good support, chipping in with two wickets, although the remaining bowlers were unable to break through. The onus now shifts to the Indian batters as they face a challenging chase of 289 to secure victory. Stay tuned...

Heather Knight, the centurion for England Women is in for a quick chat. She says that she is feeling good about contributing to the team after a couple of disappointing outings. Adds that the wicket is on the slower side and she had to take a bit of time early on. Mentions that the partnership with Nat Sciver-Brunt was a crucial one, with her being the aggressor and using the sweep shots, which is one of her go-tos. Says that the conditions are good for batting, but they didn't quite maximise the last ten overs, and they need to bowl really well. Ends by saying that they need to put early pressure and pick some quick wickets.

The momentum was capitalized upon by a formidable partnership between captain Nat Sciver-Brunt and Heather Knight. Knight adopted the aggressor role, forming a crucial 113-run partnership. While Sciver-Brunt contributed a solid 38, it was Knight who was the linchpin of the innings, ultimately scoring a magnificent 109 before her wicket fell late in the 45th over.

An imposing total of 288 has been set by the England Women's team, courtesy of a dominant batting performance. The foundation was laid by the opening pair of Tammy Beaumont and Amy Jones, who added a strong 73-run stand. Following Beaumont's dismissal in the 16th over, Jones continued for a while, eventually reaching a half-century before departing in the 22nd over, setting the stage for the middle order.

PITCH REPORT - Mithali Raj is pitchside. She says its hot and humid setting on a dry, red-soiled, well-rolled surface. Adds it’s fresh and hard, likely batting-friendly early on, with spinners to come into play as the game progresses. Says average score here is 275-plus, so a high-scoring day is anticipated.

Harmanpreet Kaur, the captain of India Women, says that they were going to bowl first anyway so they are happy with the toss. Informs that Jemimah Rodrigues misses out and Renuka Singh Thakur comes in the team. Adds that having that extra bowlers is always a great thing. Ends by saying that Renuka has an excellent record against England Women and that's why they wanted her in the team.

Nat Sciver-Brunt, the skipper of England Women, says that they will bat first. Adds that it's a fresh wicket and they'll look to put up a good score. She says that Sophie Ecclestone and Lauren Bell are back in their side. She adds that they are ready for the challenge and they have tough games left. Ends by saying they come here with confidence and they'll look to give their best.

We are down to match number 20 of the 2025 Women’s World Cup, where India will take on England at the Holkar Stadium in Indore. India’s campaign so far has been a mixed one as they began with two not-so-convincing wins but have since suffered back-to-back defeats. This contest marks the halfway point in a crucial stretch of four big games that will likely determine their qualification for the next round, and they will be eager to collect maximum points from the upcoming fixtures against England and New Zealand. In their previous outing against Australia, even after posting 330, it was not enough to win against the Aussies, and it turned out to be a tough pill to swallow for the hosts. The silver lining, however, was Smriti Mandhana returning to form. Jemimah Rodrigues and captain Harmanpreet Kaur are still searching for their rhythm and will need to step up. On the bowling front, India’s struggles continued against Australia, and with only five frontline options, the attack did not look well-equipped. Given how England’s right-handers have struggled against deliveries nipping back in, especially noticeable in their game against Pakistan, India might consider recalling Renuka Singh Thakur to exploit that weakness. Overall, opting for six bowling options could offer better balance, and it remains to be seen whether the Indian think tank will stick to the five-bowler approach or make the tactical shift. On the other hand, England are one of the two unbeaten teams in the competition alongside Australia. Despite their perfect record so far, they will feel that they have not quite played their best cricket yet. Nat Sciver-Brunt’s side has been found wanting with the bat multiple times and will want to improve significantly with crucial games against India, Australia and New Zealand coming up. In their previous outing against Pakistan, they found themselves in deep trouble at 78/7 but managed to come away with a point as the match was eventually abandoned due to rain. Heather Knight and Sciver-Brunt have been among the runs, but England will need the likes of Amy Jones, Tammy Beaumont, Sophia Dunkley and Alice Capsey to step up if they are to make a deep run in the tournament. Sophie Ecclestone and Lauren Bell missed the Pakistan game due to illness, and England will be hoping they are fit enough to return. Considering India’s struggles against left-arm spin in this tournament, the presence of Ecclestone, along with Linsey Smith, could prove crucial to their chances in this contest. Sciver-Brunt and her team currently stand with 7  points from 4 games and need just one win from their remaining three fixtures to secure qualification for the next round. Earlier this year, these two sides met in an ODI series in England, which India won 2–1. However, in the lead-up to this tournament, England claimed victory in the warm-up fixture and have also won the last four ODI World Cup meetings between these two nations. Will India break that streak, or will England continue their dominance on the biggest stage? We shall find out.
